english: Let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be a function, continuous at $x=0$, such that $f(x+y)=f(x)f(y)$ for all $x,y\in\mathbb{R}$ and $f(x)\ge1+2x$ for all $x\in\mathbb{R}$. Then the value of $f(\log_e6)$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ एक फलन है, जो $x=0$ पर सतत है, तथा सभी $x,y\in\mathbb{R}$ के लिए $f(x+y)=f(x)f(y)$ एवं सभी $x\in\mathbb{R}$ के लिए $f(x)\ge1+2x$ है। तब $f(\log_e6)$ का मान ______ है।
solution: $f(1)\ge3$, so $f\not\equiv0$; if $f(a)=0$ then $f(x)=f(a)f(x-a)=0$ for all $x$. Hence $f(x)=f\left(\dfrac x2\right)^{2}>0$ and $f(0)=f(0)^{2}\Rightarrow f(0)=1$
Continuity at $0$ spreads: $f(x+t)=f(x)f(t)\to f(x)f(0)=f(x)$ as $t\to0$, so $f$ is continuous on $\mathbb{R}$
$\log_e f$ is continuous and additive $\Rightarrow\log_e f(x)=kx$, i.e. $f(x)=e^{kx}$
$\varphi(x)=e^{kx}-1-2x\ge0$ with $\varphi(0)=0$: $x=0$ is a minimum, so $\varphi'(0)=k-2=0\Rightarrow k=2$ (and $e^{2x}\ge1+2x$ does hold)
solution_full: From the inequality, $f(1)\ge3$, so $f$ is not identically zero. If $f(a)=0$ for some $a$, then $f(x)=f(a)f(x-a)=0$ for every $x$, which is impossible; hence $f(x)\ne0$ for all $x$.
Then $f(x)=f\left(\dfrac x2\right)f\left(\dfrac x2\right)=f\left(\dfrac x2\right)^{2}>0$ for all $x$, and $f(0)=f(0)^{2}$ with $f(0)\ne0$ gives $f(0)=1$.
Continuity everywhere: for any $x$, $f(x+t)=f(x)f(t)$ and $f(t)\to f(0)=1$ as $t\to0$ (continuity at $0$), so $f(x+t)\to f(x)$; thus $f$ is continuous on $\mathbb{R}$.

Let $g(x)=\log_e f(x)$. Then $g$ is continuous and $g(x+y)=g(x)+g(y)$. This gives $g(n)=ng(1)$, then $g\left(\dfrac pq\right)=\dfrac pq\,g(1)$ for rationals, and by continuity $g(x)=kx$ for all real $x$, where $k=g(1)$. So $f(x)=e^{kx}$.

Now $\varphi(x)=e^{kx}-1-2x\ge0$ for all $x$ and $\varphi(0)=0$, so $\varphi$ has a minimum at $x=0$ and $\varphi'(0)=k-2=0$, i.e. $k=2$. (If $k>2$, $\varphi<0$ just left of $0$; if $k<2$, just right of $0$.) Conversely $e^{2x}\ge1+2x$ for all real $x$, since $e^{t}\ge1+t$.
originality_note: New: the exponential Cauchy equation with continuity at one point, where the base is fixed not by a value but by a global tangent-line inequality f(x)>=1+2x (way 5). Closest known: f(x+y)=f(x)f(y) with f(x)=1+x g(x), g(x)->2, giving f'(x)=2f(x). Different because: the student must see that the inequality touches at x=0 and forces k=2 through a minimum condition.

concept_use.Cauchy’s Functional Equations: Standard: f(x+y)=f(x)f(y) gives f(0)=1, f>0 and, via ln f additive, the form f(x)=e^{kx}.
concept_use.Continuity of a function defined by a fu: Continuity at x=0 is extended to all of R through f(x+t)=f(x)f(t), which is what makes the additive equation for ln f linear.

stem_review: Read as a student: domain, continuity at 0 only, the equation and the inequality are stated for all reals; uniqueness of k=2 checked numerically (k=1.9 and 2.1 violate the inequality). Answer 36, positive 2-digit integer as planned. Changed: No change.
key_step: Seeing that e^{kx}>=1+2x for all x forces the touching slope k=2.
justification: Two linked ideas with no options: deriving the exponential form from the equation plus continuity at a point, and converting a global inequality into k=2 via a minimum at 0. Comparable to 2024-P2-Q8 (L2, Cauchy equations, evaluate) with a genuine extra idea; below 2025-P1-Q12 (L4).
